stories.title: Postman silently auto-installs AI plugins and attempts to share all API data
stories.blurb: Postman quietly bundled AI plugins without consent and started exfiltrating API request data — including tokens and secrets — to external servers. This is a massive trust violation for anyone who uses Postman to test authenticated APIs. If you haven't already migrated to Bruno or curl-based workflows, this is your sign.

stories.title: Qwen 3.8 27B on my laptop can interpret model weights, too
stories.blurb: Simon Willison shows that Qwen 3.8 27B, running entirely on a consumer laptop, can meaningfully interpret model weights — a capability previously requiring frontier-scale models. Local LLM inference keeps leveling up at a dizzying pace. This is directly actionable if you're running llama.cpp or Ollama.

stories.title: Tell HN: Gemini trains on chat history, even for subscribers (personal accounts)
stories.blurb: Even paid Gemini subscribers on personal Google accounts have their conversations used for training — a fact buried deep in settings. If you're comparing AI tools and care about data hygiene, this is a critical differentiator. Worth auditing your team's AI tool policies today.

stories.title: AI is forcing us to pay off 40 years of technical debt
stories.blurb: IEEE Spectrum digs into how AI-assisted attack tooling is finally making ancient PHP-to-shell vulnerabilities trivially exploitable at scale, forcing a reckoning with decades of ignored legacy code. The AI coding assistant era cuts both ways: it accelerates defenders and attackers equally. Essential reading for anyone shipping prod software.

stories.title: The Internals of PostgreSQL
stories.blurb: A free, exhaustive online book covering PostgreSQL's storage, process architecture, WAL, and query execution internals. This resurfaces periodically for good reason — there's nothing else like it for understanding what Postgres is actually doing under the hood. Bookmark and read slowly.

stories.title: Kitty 0.50
stories.blurb: Kitty 0.50 is a landmark release for the GPU-accelerated terminal emulator — changelog is packed with performance wins, new layout features, and macOS improvements. If you're a Kitty user this is a must-upgrade; if you're still on iTerm2, this release is a fresh reason to reconsider.

stories.title: How I use AI (Oct 2026)
stories.blurb: A candid, opinionated look at how a working developer actually integrates AI into their daily workflow as of late 2026 — what sticks, what doesn't, and where the hype diverges from reality. The 264-comment thread is equally worth reading for the community's contrasting experiences.

stories.title: Nvidia RTX Spark encrypted firmware slows inference speed to 35% on Linux
stories.blurb: Nvidia's RTX Spark laptop GPU ships with encrypted firmware that throttles inference to just 35% of rated speed on Linux — a stunning penalty for local AI workloads. This is a significant gotcha if you're evaluating hardware for on-device model inference, and raises serious questions about Nvidia's commitment to open platforms.

stories.title: Synaptics Appears to Use Legal Threats to Block Open-Source DisplayLink Driver
stories.blurb: Synaptics is allegedly threatening legal action to suppress an open-source DisplayLink driver, locking users into proprietary software for multi-monitor setups. This matters for anyone using USB-C docks — and it's a worrying precedent for hardware interoperability rights.

stories.title: North Korean fake job interview led to $6.3B Binance heist
stories.blurb: North Korean operatives used a fake job interview pretext to plant malware, eventually leading to a $6.3 billion Binance breach. The social engineering playbook here — fake recruiter, trojanized coding challenge — is increasingly targeting mainstream tech companies, not just crypto. Know the patterns.

stories.title: New iPad mini hands-on: Refreshed design, OLED display, more - 9to5Mac
stories.blurb: The new iPad mini gets an OLED display and A20 Pro chip — a significant generational leap for the compact iPad that's beloved by developers for its portability. If you've been holding out for a worthwhile upgrade, this appears to be it.

stories.title: Siri AI is now open to all developers - Latest News - Apple Developer
stories.blurb: Apple has opened Siri AI integration APIs to all third-party developers, a potentially transformative move for the iOS/macOS ecosystem. Building Siri actions and on-device AI features into your apps just got dramatically more accessible.

stories.title: Introducing Flint - Recursive
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: local, AI, offline, inference, macOS
stories.blurb: Recursive's Flint is a new MoE coding model under 50B parameters that tops SWE-Bench Pro v2 and runs more than 5x faster than comparable dense models — with explicit macOS/offline inference support. For developers who want Claude Code-level coding assistance running locally, this is worth serious attention.

stories.title: Robert Haas: Postgres 19 is late, and it's AI's fault
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: postgres, llm, programming
stories.blurb: A PostgreSQL core contributor argues that the flood of AI-generated patch submissions is overwhelming the review pipeline and delaying Postgres 19. It's a candid insider account of how LLM-assisted development creates new bottlenecks in open-source governance — and a cautionary tale for maintainers everywhere.

stories.title: Police Chief physically unplugs Flock cameras after the company ignores contract cancellation — city takes matters into its own hands amid privacy controversies | Tom's Hardware
stories.blurb: A police chief had to physically yank Flock Safety license-plate cameras from their mounts after the vendor refused to honor a contract cancellation — revealing alarming vendor lock-in in public surveillance infrastructure. A striking illustration of why surveillance tech procurement deserves much more public scrutiny.

stories.title: The shelf life of LLM findings
stories.blurb: Researchers track how quickly published findings about LLM capabilities become obsolete as models are updated — the answer is: very fast, often within months. This has huge implications for how we evaluate AI tools and trust benchmark comparisons. Essential epistemics for anyone building on top of LLMs.

stories.title: GitHub - morluto/rea: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries. · GitHub
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: morluto, ghidra, hopper, mcp, reverse-engineering, binary-analysis
stories.blurb: REA is an open-source agentic framework that connects AI to reverse-engineering tools like Ghidra and Hopper via MCP, automating feature reconstruction from native binaries. If you ever need to understand undocumented APIs or legacy binaries, this dramatically lowers the barrier.

stories.title: boat: Cheapest, Most Powerful Sandboxes for Agents
stories.blurb: Boat offers lightweight, cheap cloud sandboxes purpose-built for running AI agents safely — think Claude Code or similar agentic workflows without the overhead of full VMs. If you're building or running agentic pipelines, this is worth evaluating as infrastructure.

stories.title: tmux cheat sheet — every keybinding, searchable & copy-ready
stories.blurb: A beautifully designed, fully searchable tmux keybinding reference — every prefix command, pane/window operation, and copy-mode shortcut in one place. Instant-bookmark for anyone who drops into tmux daily and still can't remember the resize-pane syntax.

stories.title: I discovered a sound that leaks your exact location (and it's everywhere) - YouTube
stories.byline: Pinboard Popular · tagged: youtube, osint, planes, sound
stories.blurb: A researcher demonstrates how inaudible background sounds in audio recordings carry enough location signal — via the Doppler effect from passing aircraft — to pinpoint where a recording was made within ~100 meters from under a minute of audio. Deeply unsettling OSINT capability with real implications for anyone publishing voice or video content.
